clue.text: Rely on getting energy from profound part

indicators.note: getting energy from something means extracting energy out of it, so one E is taken away

parts.note: the deep end of a swimming pool is its profound part
E is the physics symbol for energy

explanation.surface: Someone draws their energy from the deepest part of themselves.
explanation.walkthrough: 'getting ... from' removes one E (energy) from DEEP END, leaving the verb.
explanation.definitionFit: To depend on something is to trust in it or need it, a straight synonym.

clue.text: Truly does fancy jumping about

indicators.note: fancy as a verb means imagine, but here it signals that the letters are dressed up in a new arrangement

explanation.surface: Someone really does like leaping around.
explanation.definitionFit: Desultory means passing from one thing to another without method, skipping between topics.

clue.text: Newsmen out of bed for a bit of physical activity

parts.note: the press is journalists collectively
up means risen from bed

explanation.surface: Reporters rise early to do some exercise.
explanation.definitionFit: This is a floor exercise where you push your body up with your arms.

clue.text: Perhaps cursory thing which children learn

definitions.text: Perhaps cursory thing which children learn

parts.words: Perhaps cursory thing which children learn
parts.note: cursory looks like a description of hasty learning, but it is offered as a word that rhymes with the first word of the answer

explanation.definitionFit: Children learn short traditional verses; cursory is an example of a rhyme for the first word.

clue.text: See father coil oddly in sport

parts.note: FR is the abbreviation for Father, a priest's title

indicators.note: oddly suggests the letters of the word coil are set out in a strange new order

explanation.surface: A father is told to look at a coil behaving strangely during a game.
explanation.walkthrough: 'oddly' looks like a call for alternate letters, but here it rearranges COIL as OLIC; 'See' just directs the solver.
explanation.definitionFit: Sport as a verb means to play about merrily, which is what a romp or caper is.

clue.text: Source of power about player

parts.note: re means concerning or about
an actor is a player on stage

explanation.surface: Talk about a performer being a powerhouse.
explanation.definitionFit: A nuclear plant's core device generates energy for electricity.

clue.text: Become aware of renal failure

indicators.note: failure suggests the word renal breaks down and its letters are reassembled

explanation.surface: Someone is told they have kidney failure.
explanation.definitionFit: To learn of something is to find it out or come to know it.

clue.text: Reported nurse's name for water container

indicators.note: reported means spoken, so the word for a nurse is taken by how it sounds rather than how it is spelt

parts.note: a sister is a senior nurse in British hospitals

explanation.surface: A nurse's name is said to be on a water tank.
explanation.walkthrough: In British hospitals a 'sister' is a senior nurse. 'Reported' gives the sound of SISTER, spelt CISTER, and N follows.
explanation.definitionFit: A cistern is a tank for storing water, such as above a lavatory.

clue.text: Shut up in this way

indicators.note: up in the sense of messed up or amiss signals the word Shut is jumbled

explanation.surface: Be quiet, like this.
explanation.definitionFit: Thus is a formal adverb meaning so or like so.

clue.text: Huge number on the Spanish railway in entertaining place

parts.note: a host is a great crowd or multitude
el is Spanish for the

explanation.surface: A vast crowd boards a Spanish train heading for somewhere fun.
explanation.definitionFit: An inn or pub is a hospitable establishment where guests are entertained and lodged.

clue.text: Badger is most difficult beast

indicators.note: most of a word means all but its final letter, so the synonym loses its tail

parts.note: hard means difficult
an ass is a donkey, a beast of burden

explanation.surface: A naturalist declares the badger the toughest animal of all.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Badger' looks like the animal of the surface but is the verb; 'most' trims HARD to HAR.
explanation.definitionFit: To badger someone is to pester or hound them persistently, a verb synonym.

clue.text: Ship's carrying poor Pinter as these reproduce his work from computer?

definitions.text: these reproduce his work from computer

indicators.note: carrying means the ship holds the other letters inside it

parts.note: liners are ships, the 's read as a plural

indicators.note: poor means badly made, so the name Pinter is rearranged

explanation.surface: An ocean liner carries a dreary Harold Pinter, whose plays are printed out by computer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'carrying' puts PRINTE (the anagram of PINTER, signalled by 'poor') inside LINERS between LINE and RS. Harold Pinter was a British playwright.
explanation.definitionFit: Old computer printers produced a whole line of text at a time, reproducing the output on paper.

clue.text: A great deal would be needed to overcome this

definitions.text: A great deal would be needed to overcome this

parts.words: A great deal would be needed to overcome this
parts.note: a great deal reads as a large amount but means a superb bargain, the thing that wins round a reluctant shopper

explanation.definitionFit: Shoppers' reluctance to buy is broken down only by an exceptional bargain or offer.

clue.text: Coral could be Regent's Park's unusually hard type

parts.note: London Zoo stands in Regent's Park

indicators.note: unusually signals that the letters which follow are mixed into a different order

parts.note: H is the pencil-grade abbreviation for hard

explanation.surface: A zoo-keeper notes that coral is a strangely tough kind of exhibit.
explanation.walkthrough: Regent's Park is a London park containing London Zoo. 'unusually' rearranges H and TYPE into PHYTE.
explanation.definitionFit: Corals are plant-like animals of the sort zoologists class as zoophytes; coral is an example.

clue.text: It's applied to bow to get string initially in control

indicators.note: in places the first letter of string inside the word for control

parts.note: a rein is a means of control, as in keeping a tight rein

indicators.note: initially picks out only the opening letter of the word string

explanation.surface: A violinist rosins the bow so the strings stay under command.
explanation.walkthrough: 'initially' takes S from 'string', which 'in' puts inside REIN.
explanation.definitionFit: Violinists rub rosin, a form of this sticky substance, on the bow hair for grip.

clue.text: Stairs can trouble church worker

indicators.note: trouble suggests the letters of stairs can are disturbed into a new order

explanation.surface: Climbing the stairs can be hard for an aged church official.
explanation.definitionFit: A sacristan is an officer who looks after a church's sacred vessels and vestments.

clue.text: Creature is shy, rejecting success

parts.note: to be coy is to be shy

indicators.note: rejecting turns the word for success back on itself, reading it backwards

parts.note: being up, as in on the up, means doing well

explanation.surface: A timid animal turns down any triumph.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rejecting' reverses UP to PU after COY.
explanation.definitionFit: A coypu is a large South American rodent, so it is an example of an animal.

clue.text: Do better over island, having potential

parts.note: to cap something is to outdo it

indicators.note: over in a down clue means turned upside down, so the island's name reads backwards

parts.note: Elba is the Mediterranean island of Napoleon's exile

explanation.surface: Outdoing others on an island shows promise.
explanation.definitionFit: Capable means able or competent, possessing the capacity to do something.

clue.text: Find good employment for flexible suite accommodating 51

indicators.note: accommodating means giving room to, so the reworked suite holds the number
flexible means bendable, so the letters of suite are bent into a new order

parts.note: LI is 51 in Roman numerals

explanation.surface: A flexible suite has room for fifty-one guests.
explanation.walkthrough: 'flexible' makes UTISE from SUITE, and 'accommodating' puts LI inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: To utilise something is to put it to practical use.

clue.text: Cold accident can be tough

parts.note: hard can mean cold, as in a hard winter or frost
luck is chance or accident

explanation.surface: A chilly mishap can make life difficult.
explanation.walkthrough: 'tough' here is the sympathetic exclamation, as in 'Tough!', said to someone unfortunate.
explanation.definitionFit: Both are commiserating exclamations meaning that is unfortunate.

clue.text: Loss of king-buried in meadow a long time

indicators.note: buried in means placed inside, so the king's letter goes between the two words

parts.note: a lea is a meadow
an age is a long time
K is the chess abbreviation for king

explanation.surface: A king lost long ago was buried in a field.
explanation.walkthrough: 'buried in' puts K between LEA and AGE.
explanation.definitionFit: Leakage is escape or wastage of fluid or information, a form of loss.

clue.text: House heretic who lays the law down

parts.note: a house of a legislature, such as the House of Commons, is Parliament
an Arian followed Arius, whose teaching the early Church condemned as heresy

explanation.surface: A dissenting member of the House is the one who makes the rules.
explanation.walkthrough: 'House' is a legislative chamber, not a home.
explanation.definitionFit: A member of a legislature is one who makes laws.

clue.text: Find argument against potato coming up

indicators.note: coming up in a down clue means the word reads from bottom to top

parts.note: a potato is a tuber

explanation.surface: A potato sprouting gives grounds for objection.
explanation.definitionFit: To rebut is to refute or argue against a claim.

clue.text: New diamonds will make one very amenable

parts.note: ice is slang for diamonds

explanation.surface: New diamonds will make anyone very agreeable.
explanation.definitionFit: Nice means pleasant or agreeable.

clue.text: Spool to throw to waste receptacle

parts.note: to bob is to jerk or toss something quickly
a bin is a container for rubbish

explanation.surface: Someone tosses a reel of thread into the rubbish.
explanation.definitionFit: A bobbin is a reel on which thread or yarn is wound.

clue.text: Meaning to reject quotes about island

indicators.note: about here means going round, so the reversed word wraps around the island
to reject sends the word for quotes backwards, reading it from right to left

parts.note: to cite is to quote
Man is the Isle of Man

explanation.surface: Someone means to turn down citations about an island.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to reject' turns CITES into SETIC, and 'about' wraps that around MAN.
explanation.definitionFit: Semantic means relating to sense or significance in language; the clue uses the noun as a modifier.

clue.text: A course in identifying some rotten tree-trunks

indicators.note: some says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A forester is identifying decaying trunks.
explanation.walkthrough: The draft took 'A course in identifying' as the definition, but only 'A course' means the answer; 'in identifying' links it to the wordplay. 'some' picks the letters out of 'rotten tree'.
explanation.definitionFit: An entrée is a dish served as one stage of a meal.

clue.text: Maybe following the boat like a seabird

parts.note: as means like
a tern is a seabird

explanation.surface: A gull-like bird trails behind a ship.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Maybe' marks the definition as one example of the sense; astern can also mean behind a vessel.
explanation.definitionFit: Astern means behind or at the back of a vessel.
